title: Satyakama and the we of the Gayatri
word: the Gayatri and the peace chants
hook: a boy tells a teacher the plain truth, and the Gayatri's we
carry: the gayatri prays as we, even alone
tomorrow: who is the who in dhiyo yo nah: the light, or the god?

segments.voice: Yesterday, all shining is the god's light, borrowed: the Kena's gods and one blade of straw. Today, what the people do with that light.

Record a voice note alone in your room, send it to the family group, and it still starts: hey, everyone. Nani says the Gayatri alone at her window, and its verb for the people is the same kind of word. Dhimahi doesn't mean I meditate. It means we. Can a person pray alone and still say we?

Dhimahi ends in -mahi, and -mahi marks we. We hold in mind, we meditate on; some readers write may we attain. Either way, never I. That fits how many families receive the verse: not picked up alone, but given, teacher to student, at the sacred-thread ceremony. And the Upanishads tell a story about who gets let into that line. In the Chandogya Upanishad, a boy named Satyakama wants to study the Vedas, and he knows a teacher will ask his family line. So he asks his mother, Jabala. She tells him the truth: she worked as a servant when she was young, moved from house to house, and doesn't know who his father is. Just say you're Satyakama, son of Jabala. He goes to the teacher Gautama and says exactly that, word for word. And the teacher answers: only a true brahmin could speak like this. Go and bring firewood. I'll take you in; you have not left the truth. That's the we in dhimahi: a long line of teachers and students, and one more voice joining it. A neighbor tradition shares something close. In Matthew's Gospel, Jesus teaches a prayer that opens, in the King James Bible: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Said alone, it still says our. One honest difference: it calls God Father and asks for daily bread and forgiveness. The Gayatri turns to Savitr's radiance and asks only that thoughts be stirred.
screen: `-MAHI: WE.` · `SATYAKAMA TELLS THE TRUTH.` · `TAKEN INTO THE LINE.` · `OUR FATHER: MATTHEW 6.` · then, large: `EVEN ALONE, IT SAYS WE.`

segments.voice: If you say a daily prayer, say it now, slowly, and listen for its we. If you don't pray, close your eyes, let the breath settle, and bring to mind your teachers, the people who handed you whatever you know best. Let each out-breath rest on the word we.
The Gayatri and the peace chants. Today's piece: dhimahi, we hold in mind, the people's half of the verse, always plural.

howItsDone: In many families the Gayatri is taught by a teacher or elder at the sacred-thread ceremony, and those who say it alone still say dhimahi, we; traditions differ on who receives it. Christians who say the Lord's Prayer alone still say our Father. Each prayer keeps its own words and its own name for God.

original.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: dhimahi, we meditate on, or may we hold; the ending -mahi marks we.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Gayatri is a private, one-person prayer.
what it means: its people's verb, dhimahi, is a we, and many receive it from a teacher, joining a line.
what a scholar hears: -mahi is a first person plural middle ending; readers derive dhimahi from 'think' or from 'place', and as a statement or a wish.
